question.:question/worked-solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=cos⁡x$ and $v(x)=log_{8}⁡x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={(cos⁡x)}^{′}log_{8}⁡x+cos⁡x{(log_{8}⁡x)}^{′} \\  & =(-sin⁡x)(log_{8}⁡x)+(cos⁡x)(\frac{1}{xln⁡8}) \\  & =\frac{cos⁡x}{xln⁡8}-sin⁡xlog_{8}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=3\log_{4} x$ and $v(x)=\ln x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & =(3\log_{4} x)^{′}\ln x+3\log_{4} x(\ln x)^{′} \\  & =(\frac{3}{x \ln{\left(4 \right)}})(\ln x)+(3\log_{4} x)(\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =\frac{3\log_{4} x}{x} + \frac{3\ln x}{x\ln 4}\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & =(\left(5 x^{3} - x - 3\right))^{′}\log_{4} x+\left(5 x^{3} - x - 3\right)(\log_{4} x)^{′} \\  & =\left(15 x^{2} - 1\right)\log_{4} x+\left(5 x^{3} - x - 3\right)\frac{1}{x\ln 4} \\  & =15{x}^{2}\log_{4} x-1\log_{4} x+\frac{5{x}^{3}}{x\ln 4}-\frac{x}{x\ln 4}-\frac{3}{x\ln 4}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=\left(2 x^{3} + 5 x - 5\right)$ and $v(x)={e}^{x}.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & =(\left(2 x^{3} + 5 x - 5\right))^{′}{e}^{x}+\left(2 x^{3} + 5 x - 5\right)({e}^{x})^{′} \\  & =\left(6 x^{2} + 5\right){e}^{x}+\left(2 x^{3} + 5 x - 5\right){e}^{x} \\  & =6{x}^{2}{e}^{x}+5{e}^{x}+2{x}^{3}{e}^{x}+5x{e}^{x}-5{e}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=\left(4 x^{3} + 3 x + 4\right)$ and $v(x)=\log_{5} x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & =(\left(4 x^{3} + 3 x + 4\right))^{′}\log_{5} x+\left(4 x^{3} + 3 x + 4\right)(\log_{5} x)^{′} \\  & =\left(12 x^{2} + 3\right)\log_{5} x+\left(4 x^{3} + 3 x + 4\right)\frac{1}{x\ln 5} \\  & =12{x}^{2}\log_{5} x+3\log_{5} x+\frac{4{x}^{3}}{x\ln 5}+\frac{3x}{x\ln 5}+\frac{4}{x\ln 5}\end{aligned}
$$
